# Macaulay-matrix ideal membership certificate

**Method.** To show b^e lies in the ideal generated by f_1..f_r (so f_i = 0 forces b = 0), solve N b^e = sum g_i f_i
for polynomial cofactors g_i of bounded weighted degree: build the Macaulay matrix of the weighted-homogeneous
pieces, test feasibility mod a prime first, then solve exactly over Q (PARI `matinverseimage`), and check the
identity in Lean with `linear_combination` (the generator is untrusted; `ring` rechecks it).

**Pitfalls.** Certificates grow fast: Casas-Alvero d = 6 in one piece was 2.5 MB with 970-digit coefficients and
exceeded 6 GB; splitting cases on how each resultant factors (b_i^m S_i, so b_i = 0 or S_i = 0) brought it to
0.79 MB. About 1 MB of ring certificate per file is the practical limit (memory is per file). d = 7 overflowed
the exact solve (1932 x 2572 system).

**Worked example.** [FAM/casas-alvero](../../FAM/casas-alvero/README.md). Possible further use: GEO-A33.1
(parabola subcase blocked for lack of a Groebner tool; untried).
